title: Dancing before the ark (2 Samuel 6)
hookLine: David dances with all his might and his wife despises him

lines: DAVID WANTS THE ARK IN JERUSALEM.
HOW SHALL THE ARK COME TO ME?
cards: Saul is gone now, and David is king in Jerusalem. He sets out to bring the ark of God into his city: the gold-covered chest that held the tablets of the law, the place Israel knew as God's throne among them.
The first attempt goes badly. The ark rides on a new cart, the oxen stumble, a man named Uzzah reaches out to steady it, and he dies on the spot. David is shaken.
How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? he asks. He leaves it at the house of a man named Obed-edom, and it stays there three months.

teach.b: Then word comes that God has blessed Obed-edom's whole household because of the ark. So David tries again, this time with joy. After six steps he offers a sacrifice.
Trumpets, shouting, the whole city in the street. And the king, the Douay-Rheims says, "danced with all his might before the Lord." Not a dignified sway.
Leaping, whirling, dressed only in a simple linen ephod, a priest's garment, not his royal robes. Up at a window, someone is watching: Michal, David's wife, Saul's daughter.

teach.h: MICHAL DESPISED HIM IN HER HEART.
teach.b: And she "despised him in her heart." When he comes home she lets him have it: how glorious the king of Israel was today, uncovering himself in front of the servant girls like some fool.
David's answer is the heart of the story.
It was before the Lord, he says, and "I will be little in my own eyes." He'll look foolish again if that's what praise costs. Catholics read this chapter beside a second story.
In Luke's Gospel, Mary travels to the hill country of Judah to visit her cousin Elizabeth. Elizabeth cries out, why should the mother of my Lord come to me? It echoes David's question about the ark.
The baby John leaps in Elizabeth's womb, the way David leapt before the ark. And Mary stays three months, as the ark stayed three months in that house.

teach.h: MARY, THE ARK OF THE COVENANT.
teach.b: Catholic tradition draws these threads together and calls Mary the Ark of the Covenant, the one who carried God's presence.

teach.h: DAVID DANCED WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.
teach.b: You'll hear that title in the Litany of Loreto.

how: In the Litany of Loreto, Catholics call on Mary as Ark of the Covenant, and the Vigil Mass of the Assumption reads the Chronicles account of David bringing the ark into Jerusalem.

o: the curtain before the Holy of Holies
the tent of meeting in the desert

games.q: the ark comes home — tap the pairs.
p: kept the ark three months, and was blessed
a title of Mary in the Litany of Loreto

s: David danced in his royal robes
he wore a simple linen ephod, which is why Michal called it undignified.
the ark stayed three months at Obed-edom's house
and Mary stays three months with Elizabeth in Luke, one reason the Church calls her the Ark.
David apologized to Michal for dancing
he said he'd be even more little in his own eyes, if that was the cost of praise.

games.q: you're David. the ark is finally coming into your city, the trumpets are sounding, and the whole crowd is watching their king. what do you do?
o: walk beside it with royal dignity.
dance before the Lord with all your might.
games.why: he dances with all his might in a linen ephod. Michal despises him for it, and he says: I will be little in my own eyes.

practice: Picture something you're grateful for, really grateful, and let your body show it a little: lift your hands, smile with your whole face, sway, with nobody grading.
If you pray, offer that joy to God the way David did; if you don't, let yourself be glad without checking who's at the window.

wordCard.voice: ark. The chest carrying God's presence, which David danced before with all his might, saying, I will be little in my own eyes. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: chest, ark. The ark of the covenant held the tablets of the law; the Church gives the title to Mary.

carryVoice: Your line: dance anyway. Little in your own eyes, and glad. That's day four hundred four.
